results: 1. Bedside examination of cerebellar function including finger-to-nose testing, assessment for dysmetria and dysdiadochokinesia, heel-to-shin testing, evaluation for nystagmus, and tandem gait assessment
coordination examination (limb and truncal): left upper-limb dysmetria and dysdiadochokinesia; truncal coordination normal
cerebellar signs (dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia): dysmetria and dysdiadochokinesia in the left upper limb
2. MRI brain with dedicated thin-section imaging through the posterior fossa
brain MRI: thalamic lesion (tuberculoma) that DECREASED in size after anti-tuberculous treatment, with no gliosis
5. Basic metabolic panel including electrolytes, blood urea nitrogen, and creatinine
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
copper / caeruloplasmin / 24 h urinary copper: normal
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Contralateral cerebellar-type action tremor and limb ataxia caused by a thalamic tuberculoma, secondary to central nervous system infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

1. Holmes (rubral/midbrain) tremor from a structural lesion at the level of the red nucleus or thalamo-mesencephalic junction
2. Essential tremor (with the thalamic tuberculoma being an incidental finding)
3. Post-infectious / post-inflammatory thalamic syndrome unrelated to ongoing tuberculosis activity
